sections.content:
Population change in Redbridge in 2032

The population in Redbridge is projected to increase from 311,515 people in 2022 to 325,803 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 53,617 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Redbridge
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Redbridge, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 20,221, with 40,007 births and 19,786 deaths in Redbridge between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Redbridge by 6.5%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 53,617, with 226,886 people moving to the area and 280,503 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Redbridge by 17.2%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,823, with 2,908 people moving to the area and 4,731 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Redbridge by 0.6%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 49,365, with 89,105 people moving to the area and 39,741 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Redbridge by 15.8%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Redbridge in 2032

The median age in Redbridge is projected to rise from 36 years in 2022 to 37 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 13% of the population in Redbridge are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 12% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Redbridge between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Redbridge is projected to stay the same, at around 68%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 176 to 179 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Redbridge?

In 2032, 23% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 26% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Redbridge between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 7% to 6%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 10% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
